Lotan
LOH-tan
proper noun
Hebrew lotan, “covering” or “a wrapping,” the son of Seir the Horite, a duke of the Horites, father of Hori and Hemam and brother of Timna.

📖 Biblical Definition

Lotan was a son of Seir the Horite, of the people who inhabited the land of mount Seir before the children of Esau (Gen 36:20). He is reckoned among the dukes of the Horites: “duke Lotan, duke Shobal, duke Zibeon, duke Anah” (Gen 36:29). His children were Hori and Hemam, also called Homam, and his sister was Timna (Gen 36:22), the same Timna who became concubine to Eliphaz the son of Esau and bare Amalek. Thus the Horite stock of Lotan was joined by marriage into the house of Esau, and the children of Esau succeeded the Horims and dwelt in their stead (Deu 2:12), for the LORD had given mount Seir unto Esau for a possession (Deu 2:5). The dictionary records Lotan as a chief of the older inhabitants of Seir, marking how the LORD removeth one people and planteth another according to His purpose. The Horims were a real people, dispossessed in their season, even as the Edomites who came after them were appointed to judgment in their own. Lotan stands at the head of a list of vanished chiefs, a witness that the LORD ruleth in the bounds of every habitation, raising up and casting down the dwellers of the earth, and that no people holdeth its land but by His leave and for His appointed time.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The son of Seir the Horite and a duke of the Horites, father of Hori and Hemam and brother of Timna.

LOTAN, the son of Seir the Horite, one of the dukes of the Horites.

The name signifies “covering” or “a wrapping.”

His children were Hori and Hemam, also called Homam.

His sister was Timna, who became concubine to Eliphaz the son of Esau.

It witnesses that the LORD removeth one people and planteth another at His will.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 36:20 — "These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,"

Gen 36:22 — "And the children of Lotan were Hori and Hemam; and Lotan's sister was Timna."

Gen 36:29 — "These are the dukes that came of the Horites; duke Lotan, duke Shobal, duke Zibeon, duke Anah,"

Deu 2:12 — "The Horims also dwelt in Seir beforetime; but the children of Esau succeeded them, when they had destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their stead; as Israel did unto the land of his possession, which the LORD gave unto them."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A name of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses that the LORD ruleth the bounds of every habitation, removing one people and planting another.

expand to see more

Lotan is a name of the Horite register, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it that the reader who meets the name among the sons of Seir may know it for a real chief of a real people who dwelt in mount Seir before the Edomites.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the sovereignty of God over the bounds of the nations. He hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation (Act 17:26). The Horims dwelt in Seir beforetime, and the children of Esau succeeded them; and Esau in turn came under judgment. No people holdeth its land save by the leave of the LORD and for His appointed season; the believer learns to hold all earthly dwelling loosely, as a pilgrim toward a city that cannot be moved.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “covering,” Lotan names a son of Seir and a duke of the Horites in mount Seir.

Lotan — Hebrew lotan, “covering” or “a wrapping.”

He was a son of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land.

He is named among the dukes that came of the Horites.

His children were Hori and Hemam, and his sister was Timna.

The Horims dwelt in Seir before the children of Esau succeeded them.

Usage

"Like Lotan and the vanished Horims, a people holds its land only by the leave of the LORD."

"The LORD who removed the Horites and planted Esau ruleth the bounds of every habitation."

"The believer holds all earthly dwelling loosely, a pilgrim toward a city that cannot be moved."
